items.problem: Migrated WinUI 3 window renders completely blank white in the automated-capture session despite a fully laid-out UIA tree, even AFTER the agent applied the skill's documented blank-window fix (deleting <Window.SystemBackdrop>). The remaining cause is the scaffold's extended/custom title bar (ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar=true + SetTitleBar + the <TitleBar> control), which is composition-dependent and absent from the UWP source.
items.evidence: score notes migration-score.json render_status 'blank ... only caption buttons render' + parity_gate_verdict overridden by 'app renders blank'; migration session-log 3141/4895/4981 (Mica removed, validator '[PASS] No <Window.SystemBackdrop>'); UIA ui/01.json controls laid out at x=774 yet uniform-white screenshots; UWP source has no title-bar/backdrop customization.
items.root_cause: The skill's blank-window guidance (MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#system-backdrop-blank, SKILL.md, Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 Section 9) attributed the 'laid-out-but-blank-white in headless capture' symptom SOLELY to <Window.SystemBackdrop> and stated removing it 'restores reliable rendering', so the agent stopped after one fix and left the sibling composition-dependent title-bar chrome in place.
items.change: Broadened the blank-window section in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md (added anchor #titlebar-blank covering ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar + <TitleBar> as a sibling cause; softened 'restores reliable rendering' to 'necessary but not sufficient') and mirrored it in SKILL.md (retitled the section 'scaffold system backdrop AND extended title bar', added the revert-to-default-title-bar step, cross-links).
items.expected_effect: Agents that hit a still-blank window after removing the backdrop will now also remove the scaffold's ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar/SetTitleBar/<TitleBar> chrome (which UWP originals didn't have), restoring reliable rendering + parity.
items.falsifiable_check: On a re-run of a standard-title-bar UWP sample, the migrated MainWindow no longer sets ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar=true / carries a <TitleBar> control, and the parity capture shows a painted (non-blank) client area; requirements go fail->pass.

items.problem: The validator only flagged <Window.SystemBackdrop> as a blank-render risk; it green-lit a window blanked by the sibling extended/custom title bar. 'Confirm each scenario renders' is also satisfiable by a populated UIA tree even when the window paints blank.
items.evidence: Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 Section 9 grep pattern only '<Window.SystemBackdrop>/MicaBackdrop/DesktopAcrylicBackdrop'; validator reported PASS on a blank app. SKILL.md ~132/~160 'confirm content renders (controls present)'.
items.root_cause: Tooling and prose only covered the backdrop path; a prose-only fix (Tier 3) can be ignored, so the risk needs a tooling signal the agent cannot skip.
items.change: Added Section 9b to Validate-UwpMigration.ps1: WARN when code-behind sets ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar=true and/or a XAML file declares a <TitleBar> control, pointing to MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#titlebar-blank. Also sharpened SKILL.md Step 3 to state that a populated UIA/visual tree does not prove the page paints and to proactively strip composition-dependent scaffold chrome.
items.expected_effect: The mandatory validator now surfaces the extended-title-bar blank-render risk on every migration, so the agent gets an un-ignorable signal even when it doesn't re-read the prose.
items.falsifiable_check: On a re-run, Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 prints '[WARN] ... scaffold's extended/custom title bar' for a project that still sets ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar=true, and '[PASS] No scaffold extended/custom title bar' once reverted.

deferred_to_human: Tier-0: consider having the scaffold used by Initialize-UwpMigration emit a plain default-title-bar MainWindow (no ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar / <TitleBar> / SystemBackdrop) so migrations start from reliably-composited chrome rather than the composition-dependent dotnet-new-winui default.
